t.6.64.1: Seeing his brother struck down by Sugrīva, Nikumbha glared at the lord of the monkeys as though he would burn him up with his wrath.
t.6.64.2: Then the hero took up a splendid iron club, bound with garlands and marked with the imprint of five fingers, resembling the peak of the lord of mountains.
t.6.64.4: Brandishing in battle that weapon, which resembled Śakra's banner, the mighty Nikumbha of terrible prowess, his mouth gaping wide, roared aloud.
t.6.64.3: The weapon was bound with bands of gold and adorned with diamonds and coral. It was terrible, like the rod of Yama, the destroyer of the rākṣasas' fear.
t.6.64.5: With a golden ornament resting upon his chest, with armlets set upon his arms, with a pair of polished earrings, and with a many-hued garland.
t.6.64.6: Nikumbha shone with his ornaments and with that iron club, like a cloud with a rainbow, accompanied by lightning and thunder.
t.6.64.7: Struck by the tip of the great one's iron club, the knot of the winds burst apart, and with a roar it blazed forth like a smokeless fire.
t.6.64.8: Together with the finest mansions of the Gandharvas in the city of Viṭapāvatī, and together with Amarāvatī as well, along with all its dwellings.
t.6.64.10: And the fire that was Nikumbha, fed by the fuel of his wrath and radiant with the splendour of his iron club and ornaments, became unapproachable, like the fire risen up at the end of the age.
t.6.64.9: The vault of the sky, with its hosts of stars and constellations, with the moon and the great planets, seemed to spin round, set whirling by Nikumbha's iron club.
t.6.64.11: Neither the Rākṣasas nor the Vānaras could stir for fear; but the mighty Hanumān, baring his chest, stood at the front.
t.6.64.12: But the mighty one, whose arms were like iron bars, brought down an iron club shining like the sun upon the chest of that powerful one.
t.6.64.13: Upon his firm and broad chest the iron club was shattered into a hundred pieces, and, breaking apart suddenly, it looked like a hundred meteors falling through the sky.
t.6.64.14: Struck hard by the iron club, that great monkey reeled under the blow, like a mountain shaken in an earthquake.
t.6.64.15: Struck thus by him, Hanūmān, the foremost of monkeys, exceedingly mighty, clenched his fist with all his strength.
t.6.64.16: Raising it, the mighty and greatly radiant one, swift and endowed with the prowess of the wind, hurled it with force at Nikumbha's chest.
t.6.64.17: Then his skin split open and blood streamed forth, and from that fist a flame arose, like lightning flashing up.
t.6.64.18: Nikumbha, for his part, staggered under that blow; yet, regaining his composure, he seized the mighty Hanumān.
t.6.64.19: Then, in the battle, the dwellers of Laṅkā cried out terribly when they saw the mighty Hanumān lifted up by Nikumbha.
t.6.64.20: Even while being carried off in this way by the son of Kumbhakarṇa, the son of Anila struck him with his fist, with the force of a thunderbolt.
t.6.64.21: Then, having freed himself, he leapt down onto the ground, and Hanūmān, the son of the Wind-god, swiftly crushed Nikumbha.
t.6.64.22: Exerting himself to the utmost, he threw Nikumbha down and crushed him; then, leaping up with great force, the mighty one came down upon his chest.
t.6.64.23: Seizing him with both arms and wrenching his neck around, he tore off the great head of the one who was roaring terribly.
t.6.64.24: Then, when the roaring Nikumbha had been struck down in battle by the son of the Wind, there arose a most terrible fight between the armies of the son of Daśaratha and of the lord of the Rākṣasas, both seized by exceedingly fierce rage.
